_comment: Configuration for scripts/run_ratchets.py (spec S15.3-S15.7).
WHAT A GATE MAY CHECK. A property of the code that is either true or false,
and whose false case a reviewer would independently call a defect: the
dependency graph points one way, a declared symbol is used, both sides of the
protocol come from one schema, a tool description names tools that exist, a
corrective changes state rather than composing a sentence.
WHAT A GATE MAY NOT CHECK. A number standing in for a judgement. The size
gate that used to live here capped files at 800 lines, functions at 80 and
nesting at 3, and what it actually produced was code shaped to satisfy it:
an API that swallowed its own error to save a line, files split on length
rather than responsibility, and a sidecar sitting at exactly 800/800. Good
design is enforced by review and by the property gates below, not by a
budget. Removed 2026-08-02; do not reintroduce it in another form.
Two of its three limits never ran at all -- the function scanner started
bodies only at brace depth 0, and a `namespace` line puts every file in src/
at depth 1 permanently. It saw nothing in 107 of 149 files while its
self-test went green against a probe with no namespace. So the file cap did
the damage listed above and the other two did nothing, which is the reverse
of an argument for keeping them: they were never evidence of anything.
Every gate declares whether it is LIVE. A live gate must find at least
min_subjects things to inspect; a dormant gate must find exactly zero. That
second half is the important one: it means the day phase 4 lands a tool
registry, the tool-honesty gate stops being dormant BY FAILING, and someone
has to flip live:true deliberately. A dormant gate that silently reports
green is v1's `ctest -E realmodel` -- a selector that matched nothing while
printing a number that looked fine.
Exemptions are by path, and every one carries a reason. There is no
wildcard-with-no-explanation entry, and adding one should be as awkward as
it looks.
_prose_correctives_removed: prose_correctives was removed 2026-08-05 along with the corrective machinery it
policed: the loop no longer steers the model, so Agent::apply_corrective and its
case arms do not exist and a live gate over zero subjects fails min_subjects by
design. If steering ever returns, the gate must return with it -- prose-only
correctives are how v1 got 11 of 34.
_layers_comment: The dependency graph, low to high. A file may include its own level and any
level below it, never one above. A file under src/ that is absent from this
map FAILS the layers gate -- it does not skip. src/mcp was unlisted from the
day it landed and nobody noticed for that exact reason: ~2500 lines that
src/pcc and src/tools both depend on, with its include direction unchecked,
found only by diffing this map against `ls src/`.
src/mcp is L0 because it includes nothing else in src/ at all -- it is a
self-contained protocol implementation, and its consumers (src/pcc at L1,
src/tools at L2) both sit above it. src/security is deliberately absent: its
single file is scan_exempt frozen evidence, and the gate skips exempt paths.
Same level twice is allowed and means 'may include each other'.
_scan_exempt_comment: Paths no gate inspects. Formerly `size_exempt`, renamed when the size gate was
removed: the dead-code gate reads this list too, so the name described one
Everything here is code we did not write or must not edit -- vendored source,
and cook-off entrants that are EVIDENCE. An entrant reformatted to this repo's
conventions is no longer the artifact its scoreboard scored, so a gate that
made us touch it would quietly detach every measured number from the code it

scan_exempt.reason: Ported verbatim from v1 (S18). These are the falsifiers, and an entrant edited to satisfy anything is no longer the thing that was measured.

The consolidated blast-radius engine, ported from v1 unmodified. It is graded by bakeoff/blast_radius (0 wmiss corpus, 15 wmiss holdout, re-measured 2026-07-30 in this repo) and the e00_merged scoreboard includes THIS header, so editing it detaches the measured number from the shipped code. If it is ever rewritten, the rewrite must be re-scored first.
Cook-off-merged edit engine ported from v1 unmodified, so a verbatim upstream fix can land without a gate arguing with it. Same measured-evidence argument as blast_radius.hpp.

_generated_comment: Files a generator writes. Their DECLARATIONS are not dead-code subjects; their
contents are still scanned as references, and every other gate still reads them.
scripts/gen_protocol.py emits one params struct and one result struct per request,
because the schema is the single source both sides come from (S4.4). The sidecar
reads request fields by name off the framed message rather than deserializing a
struct, so the C++ mirrors are unreferenced BY CONSTRUCTION -- they exist for the
TypeScript client and for the diff. Listing them one at a time meant 16 exemptions
that grew by two with every new request, each restating the same sentence. The
property that actually guards this file is the protocol gate, which regenerates it

generated.reason: Emitted by scripts/gen_protocol.py from protocol/schema.json; guarded by the protocol gate, which diffs the whole file.

_dead_code_exempt_comment: EMPTY, and worth keeping empty. Every entry that used to be here had expired:
sixteen protocol mirrors, now covered by `generated` above as one rule; and two
whose own reasons named the condition that retired them -- SystemClock said
'remove this when the sidecar lands' and the sidecar landed, base64_decode named
a phase-2 caller and a round-trip test references it either way. Neither had
That is the failure mode of a by-symbol exemption list: it is written when the
gate is inconvenient and never read again, so it silently accumulates permission
to skip checks nobody rechecked. An entry here should be rare and should state
the condition that ends it, in terms someone can test.
